artists.biography:
The Revolution (also known as Prince & The Revolution) was an American rock band formed in Minneapolis, Minnesota in 1979 by Prince. Although widely associated with rock music, the band's sound incorporated pop, funk, rhythm and blues, heavy metal and hard rock elements. Before their official break-up, The Revolution had released one studio album, two soundtracks, and two videos. The band is known for its many members, varied in race and gender.
The Revolution rose to international fame in the mid-1980s with Purple Rain, selling over 16 million albums in the United States alone. The band achieved two number-one Billboard 200 albums (Purple Rain and Around the World in a Day), six top ten singles on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, and won three Grammy Awards. The band officially disbanded in 1986 after the Hit n Run – Parade Tour, which supported Parade, the soundtrack for Under the Cherry Moon.

perplexity.description:
Around The World In A Day is the seventh studio album by Prince and The Revolution, originally released in 1985 and reissued in 2025 by NPG Records. The album marks a stylistic departure from the commercially massive Purple Rain, embracing a blend of rock, funk/soul, and pop with a psychedelic and inward-looking sound. It was notable for its surprise release shortly after the Purple Rain tour, eschewing traditional promotional strategies in favor of an uninterrupted listening experience, reflecting Prince’s artistic boldness and control.

Musically, the album explores lush arrangements and experimental textures, incorporating diverse influences that expanded Prince’s sonic palette beyond the mainstream pop-funk of his earlier work. This positioned Around The World In A Day as a pivotal transitional record in his discography, bridging the monumental success of Purple Rain and the more eclectic Parade that followed. The 2025 remastered edition, mixed in Dolby Atmos and overseen by original mastering engineer Bernie Grundman, has been praised for revitalizing the album’s intricate production and reaffirming its artistic significance.

Critically, Around The World In A Day was initially met with mixed reactions due to its unexpected style shift but has since been recognized as a daring and influential work that challenged pop conventions. The 2025 reissue has renewed interest and appreciation, highlighting its enduring legacy within Prince’s catalog and its impact on the fusion of rock, funk, and psychedelic pop.
